sourceOccurrences.label: Canonical Bernoulli configuration law
sourceOccurrences.locator: Named statement start lines in the pinned source: 41, 47, 59, 66, 75
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Source-inspected statement correspondence with scope qualifications
sourceOccurrences.note: The introductory law construction explains the canonical product definition, weighted two-point coordinate measures, measurable identification of binary functions and open sets, and homogeneous sampling from a fixed subset. The probability-measure instance is discussed but is not counted among explicit definitions/theorems. These identities hold for arbitrary coordinate sets. The original product-model definition is linked, not duplicated or edited. The source retains its upstream attribution; no Lean source is copied.

sourceOccurrences.label: Summable profile perturbations
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Source-inspected event inequalities with additional deductions identified
sourceOccurrences.note: W90W gives both ordered-profile inequalities, comparison through the coordinatewise minimum, the full absolute-difference estimate when the discrepancy is finite, and countable bond connection/infinite-cluster applications. The cap by one, bounded-observable estimate and off-diagonal refinement are deductions. No continuity in the weaker product topology or across a homogeneous critical parameter is inferred.

sourceOccurrences.label: Left continuity and vanishing boundary flux
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Source-inspected exposition with explicit scope distinctions
sourceOccurrences.note: Left continuity allows infinite susceptibility and needs no summable-row assumption. Vanishing boundary flux needs finite susceptibility at one root and a finite uniform probability-row bound, but no transitivity. The three-way RDF0 equivalence is not exported here.

sourceOccurrences.label: Order and lower semicontinuity of connection probabilities
sourceOccurrences.note: 6B9V and ARYU give monotonicity and lower semicontinuity; RA0Z gives finite-coordinate continuity. The extension explains continuous-within lower intervals on general topological preorders, not only sequential left limits on the real line. No full continuity or critical continuity is inferred.

sourceOccurrences.label: Upper semicontinuity on a locally finite host
sourceOccurrences.note: Y5HD gives the finite-boundary escape proof and right continuity along monotone continuous families. One fixed locally finite support graph is essential; its degrees need not be uniformly bounded. Diagonal probabilities are unrestricted. The ambient vertex set is countable for the probabilistic conclusion.

proofUses.reason: Extends the finite-block discrepancy coupling to countably many coordinates; the source uses ordered couplings through the minimum, and diagonal erasure refines the bond sum.
Finite incident host edges make escape a cylinder; continuity from above gives an infimum, and ordered comparison supplies the one-sided bound.
Finite-cluster atom probabilities are continuous by the finite boundary sum. Their sum gives upper semicontinuity of the infinite-cluster probability; ordered coupling gives right continuity.
